title: Design Jev code-health checks, grounded in existing Jev code
summary: Retry of the rejected design job: write docs/design/jev-code-health.md (no code) specifying typed Jev code-health questions run in shadow mode. This time it first surveys the existing Jev client, FakeJev and scoring code and marks every build item reuse, extend or new. Audience: Sri, judging whether the checks are specified well enough to build.

defaults_applied.how: Existing-code claims cite file paths; costs and call counts are labeled estimates.
Doc is written for an outside reader, defining Jev, shadow mode and Hestia on first use.
Decision entry proposed with alternatives; not accepted.
Only the design doc, decision entry, changelog and link file change; build plan jobs each sized for one producer run.
cargo test run to confirm decision and link tests pass.
Criteria require each build item to be checked against the survey and scoring tied to measurable later evidence.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The attempt's changes were discarded, so docs/design/jev-code-health.md does not exist at base and must be created in full; the earlier content requirements still apply.

Existing code to survey includes crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs (client, FakeJev, multi-question request_body, live test), crates/athena-core/src/labeled.rs and the `athena score-jev` command (crates/athena-cli), and docs/design/defaults-loop.md lines ~640-680.
Request 20261026-042558-5p65 is not in the repo; the doc must label its deterministic measures as assumed or as an interface to be confirmed, not as checked facts.
Per-call price is stated as a range using both $0.000012 and the later estimate of about $0.00002, labeled as estimates; call counts reflect batching of several questions per call.
docs/decision-links.toml changes only if a decisions test requires a link for the new entry.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/jev-code-health.md has an 'Existing code' section listing, with file paths and what each does, the Jev client for POST /v1/evaluate, FakeJev, the live test, and labeled.rs plus the `athena score-jev` command, each verifiable by opening the cited path.

Every build-plan item is marked reuse, extend or new against that survey; no item marked new shares a name or purpose with an existing item (no rebuilt client, fake or scorer), and the batching assumption (several questions per call) and per-call price range ($0.000012 to about $0.00002, labeled estimates) cite the code and defaults-loop.md.

For each of at least five questions (one-thing-or-several, added coupling, module placement, god-object drift, duplicated logic) the doc gives the state (bounded excerpt and context), options, criteria, numeric confidence threshold, and effect (status finding, structural-pass request, or nothing).

The doc defines the shadow period, its exit rule, and the evidence scoring each question (flagged file later breaks or churns; recommended split lands and reduces churn), with how it is measured and how it feeds the existing scorer.

The doc explains fit with deterministic code-health measures (marking 20261026-042558-5p65 measures as assumed), Hestia (20261025-033743-npr5) and the scope guard, and gives cost per landing as calls times price with labeled estimates.

docs/decisions.md gains one entry marked proposed with alternatives; the build plan jobs are each stated as sized for one producer run with files and a test or demonstration; CHANGELOG.md has an entry; no other files change.
Run cargo test from the repository root: all tests pass, including any test checking decisions.md format or decision links.

out_of_scope: Any Rust code, including the Jev client, FakeJev, labeled.rs or score-jev changes
Designing the deterministic code-health check of request 20261026-042558-5p65 itself
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference because the producer must survey existing Jev code before drafting.
urgent_reason: Retry avoids a repeat rejection and redo-work by requiring the existing-code survey before drafting.
